newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran's top judge calls for crackdown on alcohol.
newsitem.headline: Iran's top judge calls for crackdown on alcohol.

text.p: Iran's top judge on Friday said police had seized a significant amount of locally brewed alcohol in a religious city, and called for a crackdown against "sacrileges" such as liquor.

"We heard of significant facilities for producing alcohol in a city with religious character. (Police) uncovered and seized a (significant) amount," Ayatollah Mohammad Yazdi told worshippers in a sermon at Tehran university.
Yazdi, the head of Iran's judiciary and a senior cleric, did not name the city or reveal the quantity of alcohol involved.
"Without government intervention, without the exertion of force, such sacrileges cannot be uprooted," Yazdi said.
The worshippers, who gathered for the weekly Friday sermon at the university, chanted "Allahu Akbar" (God is greatest) in response. The sermons are broadcast live on Tehran radio.
Drinking, producing and selling alcohol are forbidden under Iran's strict Islamic laws.
